patient.chief_complaint: Recurrent headache with aura episodes — CADASIL screen ordered after aunt diagnosed with CADASIL
patient.hpi:
A 34-year-old Polish woman presented to the neurology outpatient clinic for review after a CADASIL (Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy) screening test was ordered by her GP following the recent diagnosis of her maternal aunt with CADASIL. She has a 6-year history of migraine with typical visual aura — classic expanding zigzag arc in one visual field over 20-25 minutes, followed by a severe left or right sided throbbing headache with nausea and photophobia, lasting 8-14 hours. She has 2-3 episodes per month. She takes sumatriptan 100 mg with good effect.

The GP arranged MRI because of the family history, and the radiologist noted 'multiple subcortical white matter hyperintensities in the anterior temporal poles and external capsules — CADASIL-pattern distribution — clinical correlation recommended.' The GP ordered a NOTCH3 gene mutation test.

On careful family history review: her maternal aunt was diagnosed with CADASIL at age 52 after multiple strokes and early cognitive decline. The patient's mother (the aunt's sibling, aged 62) is reportedly healthy and 'just has headaches.' There is no known grandfather or great-grandparent history of CADASIL. The patient wants to know if she has CADASIL and what it means for her future. She is planning to have a second child and wants to know the implications.
pmh: One previous pregnancy (normal delivery, no complications)
No hypertension, diabetes, or cardiac disease

useless_tools.rationale: Head CT is less sensitive than MRI for migraine-relevant structural causes and is not indicated in typical migraine with aura; even when imaging is warranted, MRI is preferred
Lumbar puncture is not indicated in migraine with aura; reserve for suspected SAH (with normal CT) or meningitis — neither present here
Routine transthoracic / bubble echocardiogram (PFO screening) is NOT indicated in migraine with aura; PFO-migraine association is controversial and PFO closure does not reduce migraine [Charles_2017]
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated in typical migraine with aura — no role unless cardioembolic stroke is on the differential
Routine MRA is not indicated in typical migraine with aura — reserve for sudden-onset / thunderclap headache, suspected dissection, or focal deficit raising concern for vascular cause

critical_actions: Brain MRI review to assess for CADASIL-typical pattern (anterior temporal pole, external capsule, lacunes)
NOTCH3 genetic testing given confirmed first-degree relative
Once CADASIL excluded, manage as typical migraine with aura
Genetic counselling for the patient regardless of result
contraindicated_actions: Do not start combined oestrogen-progestogen contraception
Do not co-administer triptans with ergotamines
key_reasoning_points: CADASIL screening is indicated when there is a confirmed first-degree relative; NOTCH3 cysteine-altering mutations are the diagnostic test
CADASIL-typical MRI pattern (anterior temporal pole, external capsule, lacunes) is distinct from migraine-related non-specific WMH
If NOTCH3 is negative, sumatriptan can be continued safely

ELECTROCARDIOGRAM
RHYTHM: Sinus rhythm 70 bpm. QTc: 400 ms. Normal ECG.

findings.description:
NOTCH3 GENE SEQUENCING — CADASIL SCREENING

Indication: Family history of CADASIL (maternal aunt); borderline MRI WMH distribution

TECHNIQUE: Full NOTCH3 gene sequencing of exons 2-24 (hotspot regions for cysteine-altering mutations)

RESULT: NO PATHOGENIC MUTATION DETECTED in NOTCH3.

VARIANTS: One variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in exon 11 — c.1630G>A (p.Val544Met) — no cysteine alteration; not in EGF-like repeat domain; classified as benign variant of uncertain significance; not a known pathogenic variant.

INTERPRETATION: No CADASIL-associated NOTCH3 pathogenic mutation. The VUS is not expected to cause CADASIL. Family history may reflect phenocopy or different NOTCH3 mutation in the aunt (full family sequencing would clarify).

CONCLUSION: No CADASIL-associated NOTCH3 pathogenic mutation detected in this patient. The variant of uncertain significance (VUS) identified is classified as benign and not a known pathogenic variant. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: No NOTCH3 pathogenic mutation detected. CADASIL genetically excluded. VUS (exon 11) is classified as benign and not diagnostic.

output.query: CADASIL MRI anterior temporal poles external capsule WMH migraine differentiation NOTCH3

results.finding: Classic CADASIL has bilateral, confluent WMH involving BOTH anterior temporal poles AND external capsules; highly sensitive and specific when bilateral and confluent. Migraine WMH: typically scattered, non-confluent subcortical punctate lesions; can involve external capsules but rarely bilateral confluent anterior temporal poles. A single anterior temporal pole lesion is insufficient for CADASIL diagnosis. In early/pre-symptomatic CADASIL, WMH may resemble migraine-related WMH — genetic testing essential. Autosomal dominant: 50% transmission risk. NOTCH3 gene testing is definitive.

output.query: migraine prevention pregnancy planning propranolol topiramate teratogenic sumatriptan safety

results.source: NICE guidelines; AAN teratology data; sumatriptan pregnancy registry
results.finding: Topiramate: teratogenic (Category D — neural tube defects, orofacial clefts); discontinuation is required at least 1 month before attempting conception. Valproate: highly teratogenic; contraindicated in women of childbearing age without reliable contraception. Propranolol: relatively safe in pregnancy; may cause fetal growth restriction at high doses; acceptable at low doses (40 mg BID). Amitriptyline 10-25 mg QHS: limited data but generally accepted. Anti-CGRP antibodies: insufficient safety data in pregnancy — erenumab washout of 4-5 months before conception is recommended. Sumatriptan: extensive pregnancy registry data; low teratogenic risk.

output.summary: Propranolol safest preventive for pregnancy planning; topiramate contraindicated (teratogenic); sumatriptan safe during pregnancy; anti-CGRP requires 4-5 month washout

findings.description:
GENETIC COUNSELLING REPORT

Indication: CADASIL in maternal aunt; NOTCH3 negative in patient; family risk assessment

FINDINGS:
  AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT PATTERN: If patient's mother carries the NOTCH3 pathogenic mutation, each maternal aunt sibling has 50% risk; each child of a carrier has 50% risk.
  PATIENT'S RESULT: No NOTCH3 pathogenic mutation — patient is not a CADASIL carrier; she did NOT inherit the mutation (if present in the mother's lineage).
  RECOMMENDATION: Testing of patient's mother would clarify whether she is a carrier; if mother tests negative for aunt's mutation, the family lineage may have de novo mutation in the aunt.
  CHILDREN'S RISK: Patient's children have NO CADASIL risk given patient is NOTCH3-negative.

CONCLUSION: Patient does not have CADASIL and cannot pass it to her children. Genetic counselling for patient's mother recommended.

output.impression: Patient NOTCH3-negative: no CADASIL risk; cannot transmit to children; patient's mother should be offered testing to clarify family lineage

output.query: sumatriptan triptans CADASIL safety NOTCH3 negative migraine

results.finding: Triptans are CAUTIONED in CADASIL — theoretical concern that vasoconstriction of already-diseased small cerebral vessels could precipitate lacunar ischaemia. In patients where CADASIL has been excluded by NOTCH3 genetic testing, no triptan restriction applies on this basis; triptan use is otherwise per standard migraine guidance. If CADASIL is confirmed: all triptans are cautioned; NSAIDs and antiemetics are preferred for acute treatment.

output.summary: Triptans are cautioned in confirmed CADASIL due to theoretical vasoconstriction risk in diseased arterioles; when CADASIL is excluded by negative NOTCH3 genetic testing, this caution does not apply and triptans are appropriate per standard migraine guidance
